Let $f(x) = x - 3$ and $q(x) = bx +1$.  If $f(q(1)) = -3$, what is $b$?

metadata.solution: We have $q(1) = b\cdot 1 + 1 = b+1$, so $f(q(1)) = f(b+1)$. Applying the definition of $f$, we have $f(q(1)) = f(b+1) = (b+1) - 3 = b-2$.  Therefore, the equation $f(q(1)) = -3$ gives us $b-2 = -3$, so $ b= \boxed{-1}$.

What is the largest multiple of $9$ which is smaller than $-70$?

metadata.solution: Dividing $-70$ by $9$ gives $-8$ with a remainder of $2$, or $$-70 = -8 \cdot 9 + 2.$$Thus, $-8 \cdot 9 = \boxed{-72}$ is the largest multiple of $9$ which is smaller than $-70$.

If $0 < x < 5,$ then $x(x - 5)^2 > 0.$  If $x = 5,$ then $x(x - 5)^2 = 0.$  If $x > 5,$ then $x(x - 5)^2 > 0.$  Therefore, the solution is
\[x \in \boxed{(0,5) \cup (5,\infty)}.\]
